findings.message: Scope in and the acceptance criteria require tests/test_seeded_phase3_08.py to pin predecessor-test closure for tests/test_daemon_composition.py, tests/test_daemon_tasks.py, tests/test_control.py, and tests/test_mergequeue.py. The exact ownership YAML fences only tests/test_mergequeue.py, under pause-resume-activation. The other three are in neither dispatch-pause-boundary's fence nor pause-resume-activation's, yet both seeds hook squatch/daemon.py and squatch/control.py, which those three tests exercise. A closure check over the prescribed ownership therefore fails by construction. The Definition of rejected leaves the implementer with a stop instead of a buildable map.
findings.paved_road: Decide the closure at authoring time and write it into the ownership YAML. Either add tests/test_daemon_tasks.py and tests/test_control.py to the hooks of the seeds that change daemon/control behavior they assert, or state which predecessor contracts are preserved unchanged. Then make the pinned closure list match those fences exactly.

findings.message: pause-resume-activation is an activation seed. It hooks squatch/__main__.py and squatch/daemon.py, where _locked calls compose_daemon_dispatch and tests/test_daemon_composition.py asserts the composition's shape. Its fence still omits tests/test_daemon_composition.py. Section 20 says activation 'proves the real in-process production composition' through the reusable harness that scheduler-activation landed and that merge-queue-activation and rework-activation both fence. It also says later activation seeds include the then-existing composition harness.
findings.paved_road: Add tests/test_daemon_composition.py to pause-resume-activation's hooks. Its Context then gets it automatically as an existing fence path with a pinned authoring-time size, and the seeded test's ownership and Context-closure pins must reflect that.
